top_band: light tan rooftop surface with parapet rim, rug, and roof hatch from rows 1 to 31
evidence: Rows 1-31 clearly depict a lighter horizontal flat roof plane (with a parapet wall, a rug, and a ladder hatch seen from above). Row 30 is a bright highlight edge along the front parapet, followed by dark eave/cornice shadow rows at 32-33, and the darker vertical south wall with recessed arched doorway, window, and beam ends from rows 34-63.

style.evidence: While the plaster speckle and dark brown material outlines are decent, the rug on the roof has a large flat fill (12x8 solid dark red center), the arched door frame and wood planks are geometrically stiff and clean compared to the intricate hand-pixelled stonework and timber framing of the Beodeul reference buildings, and overall tile density is noticeably simpler.
